mental.title: Mental wellbeing

sleep.title: Sleep
sleep.description: Snoring, tiredness and how long you sleep.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: The wearable you use. To bring in its readings, connect it in Settings → Devices.

dateOfBirth.label: What is your date of birth?
dateOfBirth.help: Every risk score depends on age.

riskSex.label: Which sex should we use for risk calculations?
riskSex.help: The medical risk models were built from male and female data. Choose the one that best matches your body; it's only used for calculations.

country.label: Which country do you live in?
country.help: Heart risk is calibrated for your region of the world.

waist.label: What is your waist size?
waist.help: Measure around your belly at the level of your belly button. Used for diabetes risk and body shape.

neck.label: What is your neck size?
neck.help: Measure around the middle of your neck. Used for the sleep apnea check.

dailyActivity.label: Do you get at least 30 minutes of physical activity on most days?
dailyActivity.help: Walking, chores, work and exercise all count.

fruitVeg.label: Do you eat vegetables, fruit or berries every day?

exerciseFrequency.label: How often do you exercise on purpose?

auditFrequency.label: How often do you have a drink containing alcohol?

auditTypical.label: How many standard drinks containing alcohol do you have on a typical day?
auditTypical.help: One standard drink is about a small glass of wine, a small beer or a single shot of spirits.

auditBinge.label: How often do you have six or more drinks on one occasion?

conditions.label: Has a doctor ever told you that you have any of these?

bpMedication.label: Do you take medicine for high blood pressure?

statin.label: Do you take a statin or other cholesterol-lowering medicine?

highGlucoseHistory.label: Have you ever been told your blood sugar was high?
highGlucoseHistory.help: For example at a check-up, during an illness or during pregnancy.

familyDiabetes.label: Has anyone in your family had diabetes?

parentsHypertension.label: Do your parents have high blood pressure?

pregnancies.label: How many times have you been pregnant?
pregnancies.help: Only used by the experimental diabetes estimate.

medicationList.label: Which medicines do you take regularly?
medicationList.help: Add them from a photo of your prescription or type them in. Names are checked against the RxNorm medicines database.

medications.label: Anything else you take, such as vitamins, supplements or other remedies?

systolic.label: Blood pressure: top number (systolic)
systolic.help: The higher number of a reading like 120/80. Needed for heart and blood pressure risk.

egfr.label: eGFR (kidney function)
egfr.help: Shown on most blood test reports. If you only know your creatinine, enter that instead.

phq1.label: Feeling nervous, anxious or on edge

phq2.label: Not being able to stop or control worrying

phq3.label: Little interest or pleasure in doing things

snoring.label: Do you snore loudly?
snoring.help: Loud enough to be heard through a closed door, or your partner nudges you for snoring.

tired.label: Do you often feel tired, fatigued or sleepy during the day?

observedApnea.label: Has anyone seen you stop breathing, choke or gasp while you sleep?

sleepHours.label: How many hours do you usually sleep?

lastCheckup.label: When was your last health check-up?

vaccinations.label: Are your vaccinations up to date?

dental.label: Do you see a dentist at least once a year?

trackCycle.label: Would you like to track your menstrual cycle?

lastPeriod.label: When did your last period start?

cycleLength.label: How long is your cycle usually?

wearable.label: Do you use a smartwatch or fitness tracker?

wantsSync.label: Would you like to connect it when syncing becomes available?

dashboard.title: Health Dashboard
dashboard.welcome: Welcome back, {{name}}! Here is what your answers say about your health.

risk.title: Your health risk scores
risk.subtitle: Calculated from your questionnaire answers with published, validated risk models.

empty.title: Your scores will appear here
empty.body: Answer the health questionnaire and HealthNet will estimate your heart, blood pressure and diabetes risk, plus quick checks for mood, sleep and alcohol.

errors.loadFailed: Couldn't load the score calculator. Check your connection and reload the page.
errors.invalid: Some of your answers could not be used. Please review the questionnaire.
errors.unknown: Something went wrong while calculating your scores.

risk.whoRegion: Calibrated for your region of the world
risk.framinghamOptimal: Someone your age with ideal blood pressure and weight: {{value}}%
risk.findriscRisk: About {{risk}} people with this score develop type 2 diabetes within 10 years

diabetesModel.label: Diabetes model
diabetesModel.experimentalNote: Experimental: trained on one population of women, with some inputs estimated. Use FINDRISC for a validated score.

reasons.existingCvd: Not used for people who already have heart disease or have had a stroke; your doctor will assess your risk directly.
reasons.unknownCountry: We don't have regional data for your country yet.
reasons.outOfRange: Your {{field}} is outside the range this model was built for ({{min}}–{{max}}).
reasons.alreadyHypertension: You already have high blood pressure or take medicine for it, so this score doesn’t apply.
reasons.highReading: Your blood pressure reading is already at or above {{systolic}}/{{diastolic}}. Please talk to a doctor or nurse.
reasons.diabetes: This score is for people without diabetes.
reasons.alreadyDiabetes: You already have diabetes, so this risk score doesn’t apply.
reasons.womenOnly: Only available for women, because the model was trained on data from women.

assumptions.diabetesFromLabs: Counted as diabetes because your HbA1c or fasting glucose is in the diabetes range.
assumptions.statinAssumedNo: You weren’t sure about statins, so we assumed you don’t take one.
assumptions.parentsAssumedNone: You weren’t sure about your parents’ blood pressure, so we assumed neither has it.
assumptions.fastingGlucoseForOgtt: Uses fasting glucose where the model expects a 2-hour glucose test.
assumptions.skinInsulinImputed: Skin thickness and insulin are filled in with typical values.
assumptions.pedigreeFromFamilyHistory: Family history is estimated from your answer.

support.title: You don’t have to handle this alone
support.body: Your answers suggest you may be dealing with anxiety or low mood. Talking to a doctor, counsellor or someone you trust can really help.
support.helplines: Find a free, confidential helpline in your country
support.emergency: If you are in danger or thinking about harming yourself, call your local emergency number now.

risk.disclaimer: These are educational estimates from published risk models, not a diagnosis. Talk to a doctor or nurse about your results before making health decisions.

vitals.title: Your latest readings
vitals.subtitle: From the Vitals & lab values section of your questionnaire.

activity.title: Daily activity
activity.empty: Connect a fitness tracker to see your daily steps, resting heart rate and sleep here.
activity.emptyConnected: Your tracker is connected, but it hasn't shared any readings from the last {{days}} days yet.
activity.syncFailed: Couldn't sync your tracker just now. Your saved readings are still shown.

report.title: Health report card
report.intro: Hi {{name}}, here's a snapshot of your health, worked out from your HealthNet answers with published, validated risk models. Use it as a conversation starter with your doctor or nurse.
report.noScores: Answer the health questionnaire to see your scores here.
report.doctorSubtitle: Patient-reported data and risk estimates from HealthNet, for discussion with a healthcare professional. Not clinically verified.
report.doctorFooter: Generated by HealthNet on {{date}}. Self-reported answers; values were not measured or checked by HealthNet. Not a diagnosis.
report.engine: HealthNet risk engine {{version}}; scores calculated on {{date}}. Model sources: FINAL YEAR PROJECT/risk/CITATIONS.md.

labels.name: Name
labels.highGlucose: Ever told blood sugar was high

talkToSomeone.title: Talk to someone about how you feel
talkToSomeone.body: Your mood answers suggest anxiety or low mood. A doctor, counsellor or a free helpline can help; you can find one in your country at findahelpline.com.

bloodPressureCheck.title: Get your blood pressure checked
bloodPressureCheck.body: Your reading is above the healthy range. Ask a doctor, nurse or pharmacist to check it again, and ask about home monitoring.

heartCheck.title: Discuss your heart risk with a doctor
heartCheck.body: Your 10-year heart risk is 10% or more. A doctor can confirm it and talk through ways to lower it, such as blood pressure or cholesterol treatment.

quitSmoking.title: Plan to stop smoking
quitSmoking.body: Stopping smoking is the single biggest thing you can do for your heart. Free stop-smoking services and nicotine replacement double your chances of quitting.

diabetesTest.title: Ask for a diabetes blood test
diabetesTest.body: Your diabetes risk is raised. A simple HbA1c or fasting glucose test can show where you stand, and early changes can prevent type 2 diabetes.

sleepCheck.title: Mention your sleep to a doctor
sleepCheck.body: Your answers suggest a possible risk of sleep apnoea, which is common and treatable. A doctor can arrange a simple sleep test.

drinkLess.title: Cut back on alcohol
drinkLess.body: Your drinking is above the low-risk limit. Try alcohol-free days each week and smaller measures.

healthyWeight.title: Work towards a healthy waist
healthyWeight.body: Losing even 5% of your body weight lowers your risk of diabetes and heart disease. Small, steady changes to meals and activity add up.

moveMore.title: Move a little more each day
moveMore.body: Aim for 30 minutes of activity on most days; brisk walking counts. Even 10-minute bursts help.

eatPlants.title: Add fruit and vegetables daily
eatPlants.body: Eating vegetables, fruit or berries every day lowers your diabetes and heart risk. Try adding one extra portion to each meal.

bloodTest.title: Get a cholesterol and kidney blood test
bloodTest.body: Adding total and HDL cholesterol and kidney function (eGFR or creatinine) unlocks the AHA PREVENT score for a fuller picture of your heart health.

regularCheckups.title: Book a routine check-up
regularCheckups.body: It's been a while since your last check-up. Regular checks catch problems early, when they're easiest to treat.

keepItUp.title: Keep up the good work
keepItUp.body: Your answers look healthy. Keep active, eat well and update your answers after your next check-up.

errors.noAnswers: Answer the health questionnaire first, so there is something to put in your report.
errors.generic: Your report couldn't be created. Please try again.

import.title: Import from a lab report
import.intro: Choose a PDF or a photo of your blood test results. HealthNet reads it on this device and picks out the values it uses, such as cholesterol, HbA1c, glucose and kidney function. You check everything before it is saved.
import.privacy: Read on your device. Your file is never uploaded.

steps.loadingOcr: Loading text recognition (first time only, about 6 MB)…
steps.recognising: Reading the text in your image…

import.reviewHelp: Untick anything that looks wrong and correct any value if needed. Nothing is saved until you press Save.

notes.unitGuessed: No unit was printed, so we assumed {{unit}}.
notes.nameGuessed: We didn't recognise this test's name exactly, so please check it's the right test.
notes.notFasting: Check that this was a fasting test.
notes.approximate: The report shows a limit rather than an exact value.
notes.outOfRange: This is outside the expected range. It may have been misread.

import.nothingFound: We couldn't find the values HealthNet uses in this file. Try a PDF from your lab or a sharper, well-lit photo, or type the values into the questionnaire.
import.failed: This file couldn't be read. Try a PDF or a clearer photo.
import.saved: Saved {{count}} values from your report. Your scores will update.

prescription.title: Read a prescription
prescription.intro: Choose a photo or PDF of your prescription. HealthNet reads it on this device, finds the medicines and checks each name against the RxNorm medicines database. You review everything before it is saved.
prescription.warning: Handwriting and photos are often misread. Check every medicine, strength and dose against your prescription before saving. Never change how you take a medicine based on this app.
prescription.offline: Medicine names couldn't be checked right now (the drug database or HealthNet API is unreachable). You can still save them as written.
prescription.notMatched: Not found in RxNorm. It will be kept as written.
prescription.nothingFound: We couldn't find any medicines in this file. Try a sharper, well-lit photo, or type your medicines in.
prescription.saved: Added {{count}} medicines to your medical history.

list.placeholder: e.g. Metformin 500 mg twice a day

enhanced.offer: Not quite right? Enhanced reading with {{provider}} handles blurry photos and handwriting much better.
enhanced.consentBody: Enhanced reading sends this one file through HealthNet to {{provider}}, whose AI reads it and sends back the values it finds.

consentPoints.notStored: HealthNet passes the file straight on and does not store it.
consentPoints.provider: {{provider}} processes it under HealthNet's API plan, which doesn't allow your data to be used to train their models.
consentPoints.review: You still check every value before anything is saved.

enhanced.sendNote: Enhanced reading: sent to {{provider}} only if you choose to.
